title: Explain and Verify 'Disabled' Sorter Side Entries Based on CSV Phase Configuration and Phase-Based Enable
summary: Use the live sorter-side configuration/state in the OptiSweep/WCS/Robotics database to explain why a sorter side (example: sorter 2B) appears disabled: the initial CSV configuration populates the database and disables anything not in phase one. Then verify whether a later phase-based database update/script has been applied that would enable the sorter side for its later phase (example: enabling phase 4).
when_to_use: When a sorter side entry (e.g., sorter 2B) is showing as disabled in the live sorter-side configuration/state, and you need to determine whether that disabled state is expected due to phase-based CSV configuration (phase one vs later phases) and whether a later phase enablement update has been applied.
not_for: Do not perform mutating database/config changes as part of this diagnostic unless a separate approved procedure exists.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute the diagnostic by locating the sorter-side record in the live database view/table, confirming its disabled state and phase association, and checking for evidence that the relevant phase-based enablement update/script has been applied.
safety_notes: This is a diagnostic procedure. Do not perform mutating database/config changes as part of this diagnostic unless a separate approved procedure exists.
access_or_tools_needed: Robotics/WCS database access to view sorter side configuration/status (SSMS/Helix/WCS DB as applicable)
Access to configuration/phase-based update evidence (as available in the environment)

access_required: L2_support access to the live WCS/Robotics database (SSMS/Helix/WCS DB as applicable)
system_preconditions: The environment has a live sorter-side configuration/state that can be queried (the sorter-side concept is represented in the Robotics database model).

steps.title: Locate the sorter side entry that is showing as disabled (example: sorter 2B)
steps.purpose: Find the exact sorter-side record whose live status is disabled so you can validate whether the disabled state matches the phase-based CSV configuration rule.
steps.instruction: Using your live WCS/Robotics database access (SSMS/Helix/WCS DB as applicable), locate the sorter-side record corresponding to the sorter side that is currently disabled (example mentioned: sorter 2B). The sorter-side model includes a disabled/not-disabled attribute.
steps.expected_result: The sorter-side record you locate for the target sorter side (e.g., sorter 2B) shows it is disabled in the live database model.
steps.healthy_condition: The disabled state is clearly represented on the sorter-side record (i.e., there is an explicit disabled/not-disabled field in the sorter-side database model).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot find a sorter-side record for the target sorter side, or the record does not expose a disabled/not-disabled attribute in the live database model you are using.

actions.label: Query sorter-side record and confirm disabled state
actions.exact_action: Locate the sorter side entry that is showing as disabled (example discussed: sorter 2B).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Example: “that one being sorter 2B, sorter 2B is disabled …”
SorterSideDatabaseModel includes “whether the sorter side is disabled or not.”

steps.title: Confirm the phase rule: CSV populates the database and anything not in phase one is disabled
steps.purpose: Validate that the disabled state you observed is consistent with the documented mechanism: initial CSV population disables entries not in phase one.
steps.instruction: In your live investigation, use the source-backed rule to interpret the disabled state: confirm that the environment’s initial configuration mechanism is CSV-based population and that entries not in phase one are disabled until later phase enablement.
steps.expected_result: You can justify the disabled state using the rule: disabled sorter sides are those not included in phase one of the CSV-based configuration.
steps.healthy_condition: Your justification aligns with the source rule that “anything that's not in phase one is disabled” after CSV-based database population.
steps.failure_condition: The disabled sorter side cannot be explained by the phase-one CSV rule (e.g., it should have been in phase one but is still disabled), or you lack any evidence to connect it to phase configuration.

actions.label: Apply CSV/phase-one rule to the observed disabled sorter side
actions.exact_action: Confirm the source rule: the initial CSV configuration populates the entire database, and anything not in phase one is disabled.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “we configure … as a CSV file that we populates the entire database … anything that's not in phase one is disabled.”

steps.title: Identify whether the sorter side belongs to a later phase (example: phase 4) rather than phase one
steps.purpose: Determine whether the disabled sorter side is expected to be disabled because it belongs to a later phase (not phase one).
steps.instruction: Using the live database/configuration data you have access to, determine the phase association for the target sorter side (example discussed: sorter 2B being disabled until its phase is enabled; later phase example given: enabling phase 4).
steps.expected_result: You identify that the target sorter side is associated with a later phase (not phase one), consistent with why it is disabled.
steps.healthy_condition: The live configuration/state you inspect provides a way to associate the sorter side with a phase (or provides enough evidence to conclude it is not in phase one).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine the phase association for the sorter side, or the sorter side appears to be in phase one but is still disabled.

actions.label: Check phase association for the sorter side
actions.exact_action: Identify whether the sorter side belongs to a later phase (example discussed: phase 4) rather than phase one.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “anything that's not in phase one is disabled … enable phase 4 …” and example “sorter 2B is disabled …”

steps.title: Verify whether a phase-based database update/script has been applied to enable the later phase
steps.purpose: Confirm whether the later phase enablement has already been applied, which should result in the sorter side becoming enabled.
steps.instruction: If the environment supports it and you have access to configuration/update evidence, check for evidence that the phase-based enablement update/script for the relevant later phase (example: phase 4) has been applied.
steps.expected_result: You find evidence that the later phase enablement update/script has been applied (example: phase 4 enablement), which should correspond to the sorter side no longer being disabled.
steps.healthy_condition: Evidence exists that the relevant phase-based update/script was applied after the initial CSV population.
steps.failure_condition: No evidence of the phase-based enablement update/script is found, or the sorter side remains disabled despite the enablement evidence.

actions.label: Check update/evidence for phase enablement
actions.exact_action: If the environment supports it, verify that a phase-based database update/script has been applied to enable the later phase (example: enabling phase 4).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the sorter side remains disabled after the relevant phase-based enablement is confirmed, stop and escalate for deeper configuration/database troubleshooting.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “And then in a database update, I can enable phase 4, right with a phase based script.”

steps.title: Record the observed evidence and expected enablement outcome
steps.purpose: Document the diagnostic conclusion: disabled because not in phase one; should become enabled after the relevant phase-based update.
steps.instruction: Record what you observed in the live database: (1) the sorter side is disabled, (2) it is not in phase one (belongs to a later phase), and (3) whether the later phase enablement update/script evidence exists (example: phase 4).
steps.expected_result: A clear diagnostic justification is recorded: the sorter side is disabled due to phase-based CSV configuration and should become enabled after the relevant phase-based update.
steps.healthy_condition: Your recorded conclusion directly ties the disabled state to the phase mechanism and includes whether the phase enablement evidence is present.
steps.failure_condition: Your recorded conclusion cannot connect the disabled state to phase-one vs later-phase configuration, or it contradicts the live evidence.

actions.label: Summarize evidence and expected state
actions.exact_action: Record the observed evidence: sorter side is disabled because it is not in phase one, and it should become enabled after the relevant phase-based update.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “anything that's not in phase one is disabled … enable phase 4 …” and example “sorter 2B is disabled …”

success_criteria: You can point to the live sorter-side record showing it is disabled.
You can justify the disabled state using the CSV/phase-one mechanism (disabled because not in phase one).
You can identify the sorter side as belonging to a later phase (example: phase 4) and check for evidence that the phase-based enablement update/script was applied.
If enablement evidence exists and the sorter side still remains disabled, you stop and escalate for deeper configuration/database troubleshooting.
healthy_conditions: Sorter-side record shows disabled when not in phase one.
After the relevant phase-based enablement update/script is applied, the sorter side is expected to become enabled (i.e., disabled state should no longer apply).
failure_conditions: Sorter side remains disabled even after the relevant phase-based enablement is confirmed.
Phase association for the sorter side cannot be determined from available live evidence.
Sorter side appears to be in phase one but is still disabled.
escalation_guidance: If the sorter side remains disabled after the relevant phase-based enablement is confirmed, stop and escalate for deeper configuration/database troubleshooting.
Do not perform mutating database/config changes as part of this diagnostic unless a separate approved procedure exists.
